name: Zolpidem
route_note: Oral tablets immediately before bedtime; extended-release and sublingual forms exist.
targets: GABA-A receptors containing alpha-1 subunits (benzodiazepine site)

discovery.note: An imidazopyridine developed in France as a hypnotic with relative selectivity for alpha-1-containing GABA-A receptors.

tagline: The most prescribed 'Z-drug' hypnotic, linked to complex sleep behaviours
summary: Zolpidem is a short-acting non-benzodiazepine hypnotic for short-term treatment of insomnia. It acts at the benzodiazepine site of GABA-A receptors with selectivity for alpha-1 subunits. Next-day impairment and complex sleep behaviours such as sleep-driving led to dose reductions and a boxed warning.
mechanism: Zolpidem binds the benzodiazepine site of GABA-A receptors, preferentially those containing the alpha-1 subunit, enhancing GABA-mediated inhibition. This selectivity produces sedation with relatively weak anxiolytic, muscle-relaxant and anticonvulsant effects.
Its rapid absorption and short half-life aim to shorten sleep latency while limiting residual effects, although morning impairment occurs, particularly in women and with extended-release forms.

history.title: First launch
history.detail: Zolpidem is introduced in France as Stilnox.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Ambien is approved in the US in December 1992.

history.title: Generics and warnings
history.detail: Generic zolpidem launches in the US; the FDA requires stronger labelling on complex sleep behaviours and anaphylaxis for all hypnotics.

history.title: Dose for women
history.detail: The FDA lowers the recommended dose for women to 5 mg because of next-morning impairment.

history.title: Boxed warning
history.detail: The FDA adds a boxed warning about complex sleep behaviours, including sleep-walking and sleep-driving, causing serious injury or death.

safety.boxed_warning: Complex sleep behaviours including sleep-walking, sleep-driving and engaging in other activities while not fully awake may occur, sometimes causing serious injuries including death. Discontinue if a complex sleep behaviour occurs.

facts: Women eliminate zolpidem more slowly than men, the basis of the FDA's sex-specific dosing in 2013.
